title: Practice · What a business is
instructions: Answer one question at a time. Feedback appears after you submit.

questions.prompt: Maya sells a $79 invoicing guide to freelance designers and sends buyers a download link. Which correctly identifies Customer → Offer → Delivery?

choices.text: Freelance designers → the $79 invoicing guide → download link

questions.feedback: The customer buys, the offer is what they buy at a price, and delivery is how they receive it.

questions.prompt: Leo builds an app. Friends praise it, but nobody has purchased access. What has he not yet demonstrated?

choices.text: That he can build an app
That customers will actually pay for access
That the app has a user interface

questions.feedback: Positive feedback shows interest. It does not show completed purchases.

questions.prompt: A tutor identifies parents who want maths support and offers four lessons for $80, but has no way to schedule or conduct them. Which part needs work?
questions.feedback: Customer and offer are specified. Delivery still needs a workable way to provide the lessons.

questions.prompt: Which DigProg idea connects to “What a business is”?

choices.text: Customer → offer → delivery with payment evidence

questions.feedback: Keep the business spine visible: customer, offer, delivery.

questions.prompt: What should you avoid while practicing “What a business is”?

choices.text: Treating praise/likes as proof of paying demand

questions.feedback: Interest is useful; purchases are stronger evidence.

questions.prompt: How do you know “What a business is” landed?

choices.text: You watched at 2× with captions off and no notes
You can identify customer, offer, and delivery in a simple example

questions.feedback: Competence is shown by doing the objective.

questions.prompt: Which metric fits this lesson better than vanity?

choices.text: Conversations started / offers sent / deliveries completed

questions.prompt: After watching this lesson, your next step should be:

choices.text: Do the practice / quiz, then name your own customer → offer → delivery

questions.feedback: Video pairs with practice and quiz — then apply it to your idea.

application.prompt: Name your customer, describe one offer with a price, and explain how you would deliver it.
application.note: Self-check against the rubric. Different valid answers are accepted; this is not auto-graded.
